body.x: Good Air will participate in the world’s largest technology exhibition CES 2020 opening in Las Vegas on Jan. 7-10 to showcase its airborne microbial high-speed concentration tester.

Good Air has completed the development of the mechanism for measuring microorganisms, and has also completed the patent application and transfer of high-speed microbial concentration measurement kit, and acquired the original technology for it. An official said, “We have technology that is superior to the ready-made products on the existing market. We have developed this meter with the goal of creating a world free of fine dust and floating microorganisms.”

He continued, “Other company’s productstake 36-48 hours, about two days to culture microorganism when measuringairborne microorganisms. It is a matter of how long it takes to acquire data.So, Good Air has begun development with the goal of measuring data within fiveminutes in any conditions, and currently, that output is coming out."
As for future plans, he said, "We would like to acquire the domestic market first, select the Middle East, South America and Asia next, and also considers the secondary market in America and Europe."

The world’s largest IT show CES shows the trend of the global consumer electronics industry at a glance. It is hosted by Consumer Technology Association (CTA) and is held every January. AVING NEWS has reported the most news on CES, MWC, and IFA, the world's three major tech exhibitions for the past 13 years. It is sending special reporters to CES this year to report major issues in the global market and introduce outstanding Korean companies to the world.
